$urlvar=//www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/ http://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/ CFTC Revokes FBOT Registration Upon Request of CME Europe Tue, 19 Dec 2017 21:28:00 UTC http://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/pr7666-17.html http://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/pr7666-17.html The Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) on December 15, 2017 issued an order revoking the foreign board of trade (FBOT) registration of CME Europe Limited (CMEEL). Such registration permits an FBOT to allow identified members or other participants located in the United States to enter trades directly into the trade matching system of the FBOT.



$urlvar=//www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/ http://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/ CFTC Launches Virtual Currency Resource Web Page Fri, 15 Dec 2017 18:05:00 UTC http://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/pr7665-17.html http://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/pr7665-17.html The Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) today launched a virtual currency resource Web page, cftc.gov/bitcoin. This dedicated page is a central repository for Commission-produced resources about virtual currency, and is designed to educate and inform the public about these commodities, including the possible risks associated with investing or speculating in virtual currencies or recently launched Bitcoin futures and options.



$urlvar=//www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/ http://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/ CFTC Issues Proposed Interpretation on Virtual Currency “Actual Delivery” in Retail Transactions Fri, 15 Dec 2017 14:46:00 UTC http://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/pr7664-17.html http://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/pr7664-17.html The Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) today announced a Proposed Interpretation concerning its authority over retail commodity transactions involving virtual currency, such as bitcoin. Specifically, the Proposed Interpretation sets out the CFTC’s view regarding the “actual delivery” exception that may apply to virtual currency transactions. The Proposed Interpretation is open for public comment for 90 days from publication in the Federal Register.

$urlvar=//www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/ http://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/ CFTC Issues Proposed Exemptive Order to Permit ICE Clear Credit, ICE Clear US, and ICE Clear Europe to Invest Customer Funds in French and German Sovereign Debt Tue, 12 Dec 2017 20:11:00 UTC http://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/pr7658-17.html http://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/pr7658-17.html The Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) has approved for publication in the Federal Register a proposed exemptive order that would permit derivatives clearing organizations ICE Clear Credit LLC, ICE Clear US, Inc., and ICE Clear Europe Limited (ICE DCOs) to invest, subject to certain conditions, futures and swap customer funds in French and German sovereign debt.



$urlvar=//www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/ http://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/ CFTC Staff Issues Interpretive Guidance Clarifying Commodity Trading Advisor Registration Requirements Resulting from the European Union’s MiFID II Research Compensation Provisions for Investment Managers Mon, 11 Dec 2017 17:53:00 UTC http://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/pr7657-17.html http://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/pr7657-17.html The Commodity Futures Trading Commission’s (CFTC) Division of Swap Dealer and Intermediary Oversight (DSIO) today issued interpretative guidance providing that a futures commission merchant (FCM), swap dealer (SD), or introducing broker (IB) that receives separate compensation for commodity trading advice is not required to register as a commodity trading advisor, provided that the offered advice is “solely incidental” to the conduct of the FCM’s or SD’s business, or “solely in connection with” the operation of the IB’s business.

$urlvar=//www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/ http://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/ LabCFTC Director Featured in Georgetown University Law Center’s Issue Brief on Fintech Innovation Thu, 30 Nov 2017 18:05:00 UTC http://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/pr7653-17.html http://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/pr7653-17.html Daniel Gorfine, Director of the Commodity Futures Trading Commission’s LabCFTC, is featured in the latest issue of Georgetown University Law Center’s Institute of International Economic Law (IIEL) Issue Brief. Gorfine outlines details of the CFTC’s thinking and the role of LabCFTC, along with a model or blueprint regarding regulatory engagement with FinTech innovation. Readers also learn details surrounding a number of current and forthcoming LabCFTC projects to build a modern 21st century financial regulator.

$urlvar=//www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/ http://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/ CFTC Comparability Determination on EU Margin Requirements and a Common Approach on Trading Venues Fri, 13 Oct 2017 15:08:00 UTC http://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/pr7629-17.html http://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/pr7629-17.html The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) Chairman J. $urlvar=//www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/ http://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/ Brian Quintenz Sworn In as a Commissioner of the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission Fri, 01 Sep 2017 13:24:00 UTC http://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/pr7602-17.html http://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/pr7602-17.html Brian Quintenz was officially sworn in today, after being unanimously confirmed by the U.S. Senate on August 3, to serve as a Commissioner of the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), the federal agency that oversees the commodity futures, options and swaps industry. $urlvar=//www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/ http://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/ Agencies Approve Interim Final Rule Authorizing Retention of Interests in and Sponsorship of Collateralized Debt Obligations Backed Primarily by Bank-Issued Trust Preferred Securities Wed, 15 Jan 2014 00:23:00 UTC http://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/pr6826-14.html http://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/pr6826-14.html Five federal agencies on Tuesday approved an interim final rule to permit banking entities to retain interests in certain collateralized debt obligations backed primarily by trust preferred securities (TruPS CDOs) from the investment prohibitions of section 619 of the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act, known as the Volcker rule.



$urlvar=//www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/ http://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/ CFTC Staff Issues No-Action Relief from the Limitation on the Holding of Customer Funds Outside of the United States under Regulation 30.7(c) Mon, 13 Jan 2014 21:28:00 UTC http://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/pr6823-14.html http://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/pr6823-14.html The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission’s (Commission) Division of Swap Dealer and Intermediary Oversight (DSIO) issued a no-action letter that provides relief with respect to compliance with certain provisions of Regulation 30.7(c) that restricts a futures commission merchant (FCM) from holding customer funds deposited to margin, guarantee, or secure foreign futures and foreign options transactions in jurisdictions outside of the United States (U.S.) in excess of 120 percent of total margin requirements.

$urlvar=//www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/ http://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/ CFTC’s Divisions of Clearing and Risk, Market Oversight and Swap Dealer and Intermediary Oversight Issue Guidance on the Application of Certain Commission Regulations to Swap Execution Facilities Thu, 14 Nov 2013 21:10:00 UTC http://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/pr6772-13.html http://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/pr6772-13.html The Commodity Futures Trading Commission’s Divisions of Clearing and Risk, Market Oversight and Swap Dealer and Intermediary Oversight issued guidance (Guidance) today to swap execution facilities (SEFs) and applicants for registration as a SEF concerning certain Commission regulations.



$urlvar=//www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/ http://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/ CFTC Staff Issues Advisory on the Applicability of Transaction-Level Requirements in Certain Cross-Border Situations Thu, 14 Nov 2013 19:28:00 UTC http://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/pr6771-13.html http://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/pr6771-13.html Today, the Division of Swap Dealer and Intermediary Oversight (DSIO) of the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) responded to an inquiry from swap market participants and other interested parties on the applicability of Dodd-Frank Transaction-Level Requirements to swaps between non-U.S. swap dealers (SDs) (whether an affiliate or not of a U.S. person) and non-U.S. persons if the swap is arranged, negotiated, or executed by personnel or agents of the non-U.S. SD located in the U.S.



$urlvar=//www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/ http://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/ CFTC Seeks Public Comment on Amended Request from CME Group to Amend Rule 538 (Exchange for Related Positions) Wed, 06 Nov 2013 21:38:00 UTC http://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/pr6768-13.html http://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/pr6768-13.html The Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) is requesting public comment on an amended request from the Chicago Mercantile Exchange Inc., the Board of Trade of the City of Chicago, Inc., New York Mercantile Exchange, Inc., Commodity Exchange, Inc., and the Board of Trade of Kansas City, Missouri, Inc. (collectively, the Exchanges), for approval of amendments to existing Rule 538 of the Exchanges’ rulebooks and the issuance of CME Group Market Regulation Advisory Notice RA1311-5.



$urlvar=//www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/ http://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/ CFTC Issues Proposed Rule to Require All Registered Introducing Brokers, Commodity Pool Operators, and Commodity Trading Advisors to Become and Remain Members of a Registered Futures Association Tue, 05 Nov 2013 22:11:00 UTC http://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/pr6765-13.html http://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/pr6765-13.html The Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC or Commission) proposed a rule today to amend its regulations to require that all persons registered with the Commission as introducing brokers (IBs), commodity pool operators (CPOs), and commodity trading advisors (CTAs) become and remain members of at least one registered futures association (RFA).
